items.title: PoC released: CVE-2026-10053
items.description: Reproducible lab for CVE-2026-10053 (GitLab npm package-registry path traversal -> arbitrary file write as git). Vulnerable 19.2.1 vs patched 19.2.2, deterministic oracle.
items.action_detail: Exploitation is plausible and impact is high
items.ai_summary: CVE-2026-10053 is a path traversal vulnerability within the GitLab npm package-registry affecting version 19.2.1, enabling arbitrary file write operations under the git user context. A reproducible lab and PoC demonstrate a deterministic oracle facilitating exploitation. Impact includes system compromise through arbitrary file writes. Mitigation requires updating to version 19.2.2 or later.
items.why_it_matters: GitLab administrators must patch immediately to prevent unauthorized file writes and potential remote code execution.

items.title: PoC released: CVE-2026-15718
items.description: PoC exploit chain for CVE-2026-15718: SpiderMonkey wasm baseline compiler array.fill missing-sync -> invalid pointer -> addrOf/fakeobj -> arbitrary R/W -> RCE
items.cwe_name: CWE-763 Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference
items.priority_rationale: Public PoC on GitHub · EPSS 0.4% · CVSS 4.3
items.action_detail: Exploitation is plausible and impact is high
items.ai_summary: CVE-2026-15718 is a missing-sync flaw in the SpiderMonkey WebAssembly baseline compiler array.fill implementation, leading to an invalid pointer reference. Attackers can leverage this to achieve addrOf/fakeobj primitives, arbitrary read/write, and ultimately remote code execution. A functional proof-of-concept exploit chain has been publicly released. Remediation involves applying the latest browser or engine patches provided by the vendor.
items.why_it_matters: Browser operators and developers embedding SpiderMonkey should apply security updates immediately to mitigate RCE risks.
